newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end higher despite earlier weakness.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end higher despite earlier weakness.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures finished higher Friday despite some earlier profit taking ahead of the weekend, industry sources said.
"Prices have staged wide swings in both directions today, with profit taking early in the session finding buyers waiting for the dip," said Tim Evans, an analyst at Pegasus Econometric Group.

November settled five cents higher at $2.396 per million British thermal units after reaching a high of $2.41 earlier. December narrowed the gap to November to 16 cents by gaining only 2.5 cents to $2.556.
Technically, support in November was seen at just under $2.30 and then in the $2.16-2.175 area. Further support was in the low-$2 range. Resistance was first pegged at $2.43 and then $2.50.
"The strong volume traded over the last two days confirms the advance," Evans said, adding that the sharp rise in open interest is also contributing to the strength.
In Thursday's session, open interest jumped 2,954 to 135,605.
NYMEX said an estimated 44,514 Henry Hub contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 39,934.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas finished one cent higher at $1.035. An estimated 238 lots exchanged hands.

Physical prices at the AECO Hub were a couple of cents stronger in the low-C$1.30s per gigajoule as buyers replenished storage inventories that were drawn on several days ago when premature cold weather hit the province.
NYMEX November Permian natgas finished up 2.5 cents at $1.98 in response to a stronger cash market in the face of the weekend. Today's volume was at an estimated 50.
Traders reported closing most deals in the basin around $1.90, up at least five cents from Thursday.

KCBT's November contract rose in afternoon trade to settle three cents higher at $2.10. Deffereds also finished marginally higher. The East/West spread widened by two cents to 29.6 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha were up about 10 cents to the high-$1.90s.
